rationale: Build on the current Bigram64 plus QK=2.0 winner with a shared-heavy, unique-light depth change instead of another output-tail micro-ablation. This reuses a two-block encoder stem across the four encoder passes while keeping the full decoder tail, rank-64 bigram head, and current quant-aware endgame intact. The hypothesis is better learning-per-parameter under the 600-second Mac mini budget: the shared encoder weights get more gradient signal each step, artifact pressure drops materially, compile shapes stay fixed, and the saved bytes are spent preserving the same proven projection-only tail path rather than introducing a weaker new head.
title: Shared Encoder Stem On Bigram64 Best
